c.tagline: Rajasthan's 'City of Lakes' — palaces, ghats, and sunset boat rides on Lake Pichola.

taxi.fareNote: Auto-rickshaws rarely use meters — agree a fare first (short hops ₹50-100) or book via Uber/Ola for fixed pricing.

emergency.note: 112 is India's unified emergency number; 100 (police) and 108 (ambulance) also work.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Touts and commission scams around the palace/lake and markets

hood_desc: The heart of the old city on the east bank of Lake Pichola, a warren of narrow lanes and converted havelis right below the City Palace and the Jagdish Temple; rooftop lake-view restaurants and the main pick for first-timers and backpackers.
The quieter west bank across the Daiji footbridge, an artier, more laid-back cluster of guesthouses, cafes and yoga spots with classic sunset views of the City Palace and the Lake Palace.
The bustling old-city core around the Jagdish Temple, Gangaur Ghat and the City Palace entrance, packed with bazaars, street food and puppet-show culture; central and lively but crowded.
An upscale, greener district around the second big lake north of the old city, with the Nehru Garden island, Moti Magri hill and higher-end lakeside hotels; calmer and more spacious.
The modern commercial part of town around Chetak Circle and Sukhadia Circle, with shopping, everyday services and business hotels away from the tourist ghats; practical rather than scenic.

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water only; avoid tap water and street ice.

transit.hours: City buses and shared autos run roughly 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; auto-rickshaws and app cabs are available later.
transit.note: Udaipur has no metro or tram; getting around means auto-rickshaws (tuk-tuks), city and mini buses, app cabs (Uber/Ola), and boats on Lake Pichola. The old city around the ghats is best on foot.
transit.pay: Pay autos and buses in cash; agree auto fares up front or use Uber/Ola for metered pricing.

bus: RSRTC intercity coaches to Jaipur, Jodhpur, Mount Abu, Ahmedabad and Delhi
ferry: Lake Pichola tourist boats (City Palace jetty to Jag Mandir / Lake Palace)
train: Udaipur City railway station with trains to Jaipur, Delhi, Ahmedabad and Mumbai

transit.m: Prepaid taxi to city center (~45-60 min)
Uber/Ola cab to the lakes (~45-60 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; ₹50-100 or about 5-10% for good service and hotel staff is appreciated.

food.name: Dal baati churma
food.desc: Rajasthan's defining plate: hard-baked wheat balls cracked open and drowned in ghee, eaten with spiced lentils and sweet crushed churma.

places.name: Krishna Dal Bati Restro
places.note: Short menu built around unlimited dal, baati, churma and boondi raita at a very low fixed price.

places.name: Natraj Dining Hall
places.note: Long-running unlimited Rajasthani-Gujarati thali hall packed with local families at lunch.

places.name: Jajmaan Restaurant
places.note: Traditional Mewari kitchen known for cooking the classics to old family recipes.

food.name: Gatte ki sabzi
food.desc: Steamed gram-flour dumplings simmered in a tangy yoghurt and chilli gravy - desert cooking built for a place with little fresh vegetable.

places.name: Natraj Dining Hall
places.note: Appears on the unlimited thali; refills keep coming until you wave them off.

places.name: Jajmaan Restaurant
places.note: Cooks gatte, ker sangri and dal baati in the traditional Mewari style.

places.name: Khamma Ghani Restaurant
places.note: Lakefront dining room where the Rajasthani vegetarian dishes are the strongest part of the menu.

food.name: Laal maas
food.desc: Fiery Mewari mutton curry stained deep red with Mathania chillies - a royal hunting dish, and the exception in a mostly vegetarian city.

places.name: Khamma Ghani Restaurant
places.note: Diners consistently single out the laal maas here, eaten with a view of the lake.

places.name: Ambrai
places.note: Famous terrace facing the City Palace across the water; classic Rajasthani meat dishes at dinner.

places.name: Poppy by Royal Repast
places.note: Heritage kitchen run by the Bedla family blending Rajasthani classics with continental plates.

food.name: Mawa kachori
food.desc: A festive sweet kachori: crisp fried pastry stuffed with milk solids, nuts and cardamom, then soaked in sugar syrup.

places.name: Jagdish Misthan Bhandar
places.note: Landmark sweet shop locals treat as the default for mawa kachori and mithai.

places.name: Bapu Bazar sweet shops
places.note: A run of halwais on the same street, all frying kachoris fresh through the day.

places.name: Hathi Pol market stalls
places.note: Old-city sweet stalls near the palace gate, good for a single kachori rather than a box.

food.name: Pyaaz kachori and mirchi vada
food.desc: Savoury street snacks: flaky pastry packed with spiced onion, and a whole green chilli stuffed with potato and deep fried in gram batter.

places.name: Jagdish Misthan Bhandar
places.note: Savoury counter turns out kachoris and vadas hot from mid-morning onward.

places.name: Manoj Prakash stall
places.note: Well-known street stall serving daal baati, daal poori and kachoris to a steady local queue.

places.name: Chetak Circle food stalls
places.note: Evening cluster of snack carts popular with Udaipur residents rather than tourists.

food.name: Ker sangri
food.desc: Dried desert berries and bean pods rehydrated and tempered with chilli, asafoetida and mango powder; sharp, chewy and purely Rajasthani.

places.name: Natraj Dining Hall
places.note: Part of the rotating thali spread and a good way to try it without ordering a whole dish.

places.name: Jajmaan Restaurant
places.note: Keeps the desert vegetable dishes on the menu year-round.

places.name: Khamma Ghani Restaurant
places.note: Serves ker sangri within its Rajasthani thali alongside gatte and dal baati.

food.name: Makhaniya lassi and chaas
food.desc: Thick saffron-and-cardamom sweet lassi topped with butter, or salted cumin chaas buttermilk - the everyday answer to Rajasthan's heat.

places.name: Jagdish Misthan Bhandar
places.note: Sweet shops here serve tall glasses of makhaniya lassi with a layer of malai on top.

places.name: Natraj Dining Hall
places.note: Chaas is poured freely with the thali, and lassi can be added on.

places.name: Bapu Bazar lassi stalls
places.note: Row of small stalls churning fresh curd all day; cheapest and often the best.

food.name: Masala chai
food.desc: Strong milky tea boiled with ginger, cardamom and clove, poured from roadside stalls at ghats and market corners all day long.

places.name: Chai stalls at Gangaur Ghat
places.note: Small carts by the ghat steps; a cup here at sunrise over Lake Pichola is the local ritual.

places.name: Chetak Circle food stalls
places.note: Busy evening tea carts serving office workers and students.

places.name: Hathi Pol market stalls
places.note: Tea glasses poured beside the sweet stalls in the old bazaar.

landmarks: City Palace
A majestic granite-and-marble complex towering over Lake Pichola, its courtyards, mirrored halls and peacock mosaics embody four centuries of Mewar royal splendour.
Lake Pichola
Udaipur's shimmering centrepiece, an artificial lake from 1362 whose sunset boat rides glide past ghats, island palaces and the whitewashed old city.
Lake Palace (Jag Niwas)
A dreamlike white-marble palace appearing to float on Lake Pichola, this 18th-century royal summer retreat is now one of the world's most romantic hotels.
Jag Mandir
An island pleasure palace ringed by carved stone elephants, where Mughal prince Shah Jahan sheltered and reputedly found inspiration for the Taj Mahal.
Jagdish Temple
A soaring 17th-century Indo-Aryan temple to Vishnu in the old city, its pyramidal spire and friezes of dancers and elephants alive with devotional energy.
Monsoon Palace (Sajjangarh)
Perched on a Aravalli hilltop above the city, this 19th-century royal retreat delivers Udaipur's most spectacular sunset panorama over lakes and mountains.
Saheliyon-ki-Bari (Garden of the Maidens)
An elegant 18th-century pleasure garden of lotus pools, marble kiosks and rain-mimicking fountains, built for the queen's ladies-in-waiting.
Bagore Ki Haveli
A restored 18th-century lakeside mansion of 138 rooms, its museum of costumes and puppets comes alive each evening with the Dharohar folk-dance show.
Fateh Sagar Lake
A breezy blue lake ringed by hills and promenades, its island Nehru Park and pearl-grey waters make it Udaipur's favourite evening escape.
Ambrai Ghat (Manjhi Ghat)
The classic photographer's vantage on Lake Pichola's western shore, framing the City Palace, ghats and Lake Palace in one glorious waterfront tableau.

train.note: No international trains. Udaipur City station is about 3 km from the lake and old city, with overnight trains to Delhi (roughly 12 hours) and services to Jaipur, Ahmedabad and Mumbai. The line was converted to broad gauge relatively recently, so frequencies are lower than in the rest of Rajasthan - book on IRCTC 60 days ahead.

bus.note: No international coaches. RSRTC (https://rsrtconline.rajasthan.gov.in/) and private Volvo sleepers run from Udaipur City bus stand to Jodhpur (about 6 hours), Jaipur (7-8), Ahmedabad (5) and Mount Abu, bookable through redBus (https://www.redbus.in/). Buses are often quicker than the train on the Rajasthan routes.

ferry.note: Udaipur is inland and has no ferries. Boats do cross Lake Pichola to Jag Mandir and the Lake Palace, run by the City Palace and the hotels, but these are sightseeing and hotel-guest launches rather than public transport.

half.name: Ranakpur
half.blurb: Ranakpur has an elaborately carved marble Jain temple complex with over a thousand intricately sculpted pillars.

half.name: Kumbhalgarh Fort
half.blurb: Kumbhalgarh Fort sits on a hilltop with one of the longest fortified walls in the world, built by Rana Kumbha.

half.name: Eklingji Temple
half.blurb: Eklingji is a walled temple complex dedicated to Shiva, historically the guardian deity of Udaipur's Mewar rulers.

half.name: Nathdwara
half.blurb: Nathdwara is a pilgrimage town centered on the Shrinathji temple, a major Krishna shrine for Vaishnav devotees.

full.name: Chittorgarh Fort
full.blurb: Chittorgarh Fort is India's largest fort complex, with palace ruins, towers and temples spread across a long hilltop plateau.
